description:
Search the world named by your API-Key header for elements whose name or
text fields (description and each type's prose fields, such as a
Character's background) hold every word of `query` as a whole word,
ignoring case: "ore" does not find "more", and "copper mine" needs both
words somewhere in the element. No stemming.

`query` is 2 to 200 characters. Optional `type` (a slug from
`list_element_types`) searches one type only; `limit` (default 50, clamped
to 1-200) caps the results. Name matches come first, then the rest, each by
type and then by name. Returns `{query, results: [{type, id, name,
supertype, subtype, field, snippet}, ...], count, truncated}`: `field` is
where the words were found (`name` or a text field), `snippet` up to 160
characters of it around the first match, and `truncated` true when more
matched than `limit` (no further pages: narrow the query). `id` is a UUID;
call `get_element(type, id)` for the full body. Requires a READ or WRITE
API-Key; a guest key searches only what it may read. This mirrors
`GET /api/v2/search`, except that a parlor's room elements (marked
`x_room_of`) and the world's reading aids (its Charter, Guide and Domains,
marked `x_charter_of`) are left out unless `include_room` is true, and proposed
elements are too. An element carrying x_review_proposed is proposed, not
yet reviewed by a keeper; it is left out unless asked for. Any value but
null counts, an object or not. `include_proposed` true keeps it, its row
carrying `x_review_proposed`: treat it as proposed, not yet reviewed, never
as a fact. A stub's row (`known_of`) of a proposed element shows no mark:
its being served under `include_proposed` is the sign.
`proposed_left_out` says how many matching elements were left out (0 with
`include_proposed`).

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. Signed in through a hosted client (a bearer), name one of list_worlds; with one world it may be left out. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world).

name: search_elements
